newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST-Japan Feb industrial output seen down.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Japan Feb industrial output seen down.

text.p: Japan's industrial output for February is expected to show a month-on-month fall of 3.3 percent, in reaction to a strong rise in January, an average of economists' forecasts showed.
Economists surveyed by Reuters predicted a decline of between 2.6 and 3.6 percent, against a hefty 5.6 percent rise in January.
Industrial output data for February will be released by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT) on Friday.
"The figure will be a minus due to the strong January number," said Yoshito Sakakibara, an economist at Salomon Brothers Asia.
MITI, in releasing the January data, had also forecast a decline of 3.3 percent for manufacturers' output in February.

A sharp increase in car production, backed by strong sales ahead of April's planned increase in the national sales tax, had boosted overall output in January, but manufacturers will cut down on production in reaction to that, economists said.
"There are already signs that the 'rush in' buying (ahead of the tax rise) is losing speed," said Salomon's Sakakibara.
The government plans to raise the consumption tax to five percent from three percent in April.
